title: Summary table claims k~log* n for (f),(g) but body proves only O(log* n)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Internal inconsistency / unproven asymptotic for families (f) Bernoulli and (g) Mersenne.**

In the body, family (g) is proved only to satisfy $k(n)=O(\log^* n)$ ('Lemma rates(L) used as an upper bound'), and the text explicitly disclaims a lower bound. Family (f) likewise proves only $k(n)=O(\log^* n)$ and states 'we do not assert a matching lower bound'.

**However, the final Conclusion table writes '(f) $k\sim\log^* n$' and '(g) $k\sim\log^*_2 n$'**, where $\sim$ means $(1+o(1))$. An $O(\cdot)$ upper bound is being presented as a tight asymptotic equivalence. This is a contradiction with the body.

Moreover the equivalence is likely FALSE: in both families $N(x)=o(\log x)$ (Mersenne $N(x)=\pi(\log_2 x)\sim \log x/((\log2)\log\log x)$; Bernoulli $N(x)\sim\log x/(2\log\log x)$), so each iteration contracts strictly faster than a single logarithm, suggesting $k(n)=o(\log^* n)$. 

Required fix: either supply a genuine two-sided estimate for the iteration of a $\log x/\log\log x$-type map and determine the true order, or downgrade the table entries to $k(n)=O(\log^* n)$ to match the body. The claim $k\sim\log^* n$ must not stand unproved.
